h: רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ אֲדָר, מַאֲמָר ו׳ Rosh Chodesh Adar — Maamar Vav

p: In Sefer Yetzirah, for each month the wording is:
"He made such-and-such letter king over such-and-such power."
that the power be on the side of the good mode,
שֶׁכָּל הַכֹּחוֹת יֵשׁ בְּטוֹב וּבְהֶפֶךְ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם.
for every power exists both in good and in the opposite, chas v'shalom.
So too regarding the month of Adar he said:
"He made the letter kuf king over laughter...,
That is, there is a kind of joy and laughter
"Of laughter I said, it is madness,
and of joy, what does it accomplish?"
And He made the kuf king
so that it be good joy and laughter.
Likewise the letter kuf that we cited (in the previous maamar)
דְּאָמַר דְּאָת ק׳ לָא מִתְיַישְּׁבָא בְּדוּכְתָּא
which says that the letter kuf does not settle in its place,
'A slanderous man shall not be established in the land'" —
that is, it alludes to the serpent,
וְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב קנב, א)
And it states in the holy Zohar (II, 152a)
that the letter kuf rules in the place of Gehinnom.
And the serpent is the one that brought sadness into the world:
"in sadness you shall eat of it" (ibid. 17).
And joy is the opposite of sadness,
יִשְׂמַח יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּעוֹשָׂיו וְגוֹמֵר [שָׁם קמט, ב]
יִשְׂמַח לֵב מְבַקְשֵׁי ה׳ [שָׁם קה, ג]
"Let the heart of those who seek Hashem rejoice" (ibid. 105:3):
when he merely seeks to attain
the light and holiness of Hashem,
even though he has not yet merited to attain it,
nevertheless he merits the aspect of joy.
But the essence of joy is "for the upright of heart, joy":
when one merits to straighten the heart,
that it be one heart to his Father in Heaven;
and when one merits the revelation of Atika,
when he is bound to the root,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ עַל מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת ל, ב)
as we said on what they said (Berachos 30b):
And regarding this month it is written (Esther 8:16),
which is called orah, in the feminine form,
for it receives the light from Torah she'b'ksav.
"Whoever engages in the dew of Torah,
the dew of Torah revives him";
and the intent of both is one:
שֶׁהוּא טַל שֶׁעָתִיד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
which is the dew with which HaKadosh Baruch Hu will in the future
and this is the dew of Torah she'b'al peh,
as is evident in the Gemara (Shabbos 88b),
that their souls departed at the light of Torah she'b'ksav,
and with dew He revived them; see there.
in which there is a shining forth of the light "that it was good,"
וּמוֹרֶה גַּם כֵּן עַל אוֹר הַגָּנוּז
and it also indicates the hidden light,
the upper tip of the yud,
as we said (in the previous maamar);
and joy is the opposite of the sadness of the yetzer hara.
גַּם כֵּן מוֹרֶה שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל קְשׁוּרִים בַּשֹּׁרֶשׁ
which also indicates that Yisrael are bound to the root,
for we circumcise an infant eight days old,
without his own knowledge, and he becomes a Jew
וְנִכְלָל בִּכְלַל וְעַמֵּךְ כּוּלָּם וְגוֹמֵר [יְשַׁעְיָה ס, כא]
and is included among "And Your people are all..." (Yeshayah 60:21),
for whoever is circumcised is called a tzaddik
like one who finds great spoil";
and this indicates the holiness of milah,
which comes by way of a find,
not through toil and the customary order.
"And honor — these are the tefillin of the head,"
שֶׁמּוֹרֶה גַּם כֵּן עַל שֶׁקְּשׁוּרִים בַּשֹּׁרֶשׁ
which also indicates that they are bound to the root
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר הִמְלִיךְ אוֹת ק׳ בִּשְׂחוֹק
This is what it says, "He made the kuf king over laughter":
that it be the good kuf,
וְלֹא ק׳ שֶׁל אִישׁ לָשׁוֹן וְגוֹמֵר
and not the kuf of "a slanderous man...,"
that is, the serpent, which brought sadness and grief.
in the manner of the verse (Tehillim 126:2),
"Then our mouth will be filled with laughter":
when one merits the revelation of the aspect of Atika,
it is permitted even to fill one's mouth with laughter
The twelve months of the year
מְיוּחָסִים לִשְׁנֵים עָשָׂר שְׁבָטִים [תַּנְחוּמָא וַיְחִי טו]
are associated with the twelve tribes (Tanchuma, Vayechi 15),
and the Arizal counted them in the order of the banners
and in this world there is no satiation,
"One who loves money will not be sated with money,"
with half his desire in his hand...";
that Hashem Yisbarach bestows will upon him,
and through this he is sated;
and so it states (Sifrei, V'Zos HaBerachah 14):
מְלַמֵּד שֶׁהָיָה נַפְתָּלִי שָׂמֵחַ בְּחֶלְקוֹ וְכוּלֵּי.
"This teaches that Naftali was happy with his portion..."
כָּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ נַחַת רוּחַ בְּעָשְׁרוֹ
Whoever has contentment in his wealth";
and Rashi explained: happy with his portion...;
as in the wording of the Mishnah in Avos (4:1):
"Who is wealthy? One who is happy with his portion."
"And satisfies every living thing with will":
הַהוּא רָצוֹן דְּאִשְׁתְּכַח מֵעַתִּיקָא קַדִּישָׁא וְכוּלֵּי
That will which is found from the Holy Atika..."
For the first attribute, Atika Kaddisha,
and corresponding to it is the utterance "Bereishis,"
in which "And He said" is not written,
for there is no grasp of it at all,
and it is hidden from all thought;
and it is the Supernal Will.
For the beginning of the revelation of Creation
is from the utterance "Let there be light,"
so that there be some grasp
from the aspect of Chochmah, ko'ach mah.
for all blessings are included in these three —
which depend not on merit but on mazal
and the holy Mazla is Atika
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג עט, ב
and since he is sated with will from Atika,
he is full of Hashem's blessing.
בִּרְכַּת ה׳ הִיא תַעֲשִׁיר [מִשְׁלֵי י, כב]
that "The blessing of Hashem, it makes rich" (Mishlei 10:22)
refers to the day of Shabbos,
And it is written (ibid.), "And He adds no sadness with it":
for on the day of Shabbos there is no dominion for the serpent,
which brought sadness into the world.
and a hundred fields and a hundred servants...,
The number one hundred that he said
is according to what they said
that Lavan would find, on account of Yaakov,
וּמְאָה אִמְּרִין וּמְאָה עִזִּין עַיֵּין שָׁם
a hundred lambs and a hundred goats; see there.
And he holds that Hashem's blessing is a hundred.
וְכֵן עֶשֶׂר סְפִירוֹת כְּשֶׁכָּל אֶחָד כָּלוּל מֵעֶשֶׂר
So too the ten sefiros, when each one is comprised of ten,
up to Atika, make a hundred
(as explained at the end of maamar 4).
And when he has a hundred of every kind
and a hundred servants to work them,
וְהוּא יִהְיֶה פָּנוּי לַעֲמָלָהּ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה
and he is free for the toil of Torah,
he is wealthy, full of Hashem's blessing.
This is what he said, "and it reigns over laughter":
since he merits will from Atika,
הוּא בִּבְחִינַת אָ״ז יִמָּלֵא שְׂחוֹק פִּינוּ.
he is in the aspect of "Then our mouth will be filled with laughter."
וּבֶאֱמֶת פָּסוּק פּוֹתֵחַ אֶת יָדֶךָ צָרִיךְ פֵּירוּשׁ
In truth, the verse "You open Your hand" requires explanation,
for it begins in the third person, "opens";
"Your hand" is in the second person;
and "satisfies" is in the third person.
"You open Your hand and You satisfy every...."
But it seems that it refers back
"The eyes of all look hopefully to You...";
that the one who trusts in Hashem and hopes to You —
וְזֶה גַּם כֵּן עֵסֶק חֹדֶשׁ זֶה
This too is the work of this month:
[שַׁעַר הַכַּוָּנוֹת דְּרוּשֵׁי תְּפִלַּת הַשַּׁחַר דְּרוּשׁ א]
דְּרָאשֵׁי תֵּיבוֹת פּוֹתֵחַ אֶת יָדֶךָ פַּאִ״י
that the first letters of "Posei'ach es yadecha," Pai,
equal in gematria Havayah and Adnus.
And this stands against and opposite the kelipah of Amalek,
דְּאִיתָא (תַּנְחוּמָא תֵּצֵא יא וְשׁוֹחֵר טוֹב תְּהִלִּים ט)
as it states (Midrash Tanchuma, Teitzei 11, and Shocher Tov, Tehillim 9),
that as long as Amalek is in the world
אֵין הַשֵּׁם שָׁלֵם וְאֵין הַכִּסֵּא שָׁלֵם
the Name is not whole and the Throne is not whole.
וְהַיְינוּ דִּבְכִסֵּא חָסֵר אָלֶ״ף פֶּלֶ״א עֶלְיוֹן
That is, in the Throne the aleph, the supernal Pele, is lacking;
and the Ancient of Days sat";
and when the aleph, the supernal Pele, is hidden,
as it were, there is none sitting on the Throne.
And the Name is not whole,
for the union of Yud-Heh with Vav-Heh is lacking.
And one who trusts in Hashem brings about the union
and the revelation of will from Atika, as mentioned above.
This is why it says that Adar was given to Naftali —
for the reason that he is "sated with will"
וְעַל כֵּן מוֹלֵךְ עַל הַשְּׂחוֹק כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
and therefore it reigns over laughter, as mentioned above.
And he is "full of Hashem's blessing,"
which alludes to the day of Shabbos,
as they said in Bereishis Rabbah;
and Shabbos is the time for the obliteration of Amalek,
and we say (Shacharis of Shabbos, Birkas Yotzer),
and sat on His Throne of Glory,"
for then is the revelation of Atika.
Therefore we say on Motzaei Shabbos
all of which indicate the revelation of Atika,

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Resisei Layla 53:1 — “Joy is only in the blessed God, in a person’s attachment to Him. Even if he is not yet attached, even if he is completely distant, nevertheless, if he seeks Him and desires to attach himself to Him, it is said, ‘Let the heart of those who seek the Lord rejoice.’ Through the light of Torah and the lamp of the commandment he can merit this joy as well.... The straightness of the heart is simply wholeheartedness with the Lord his God: knowing that there is a Creator and Governor and that nothing exists apart from Him. This straightens every crookedness of the heart.”

paragraphs.text: Connection: This explains why the maamar locates joy already in seeking God, before attainment is complete: seeking is rooted in an existing faith that can straighten the heart. The parallel distinguishes that inward joy from the full illuminating clarity attained through righteous action.

paragraphs.text: Shabbat 88b — “Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: With every utterance that came from the mouth of the Holy One, blessed be He, the souls of Israel departed, as it is said, ‘My soul departed when He spoke.’ If their souls departed at the first utterance, how did they receive the second? He brought down the dew with which He will revive the dead in the future and revived them, as it is said, ‘You showered abundant rain, O God; when Your inheritance was weary, You sustained it.’”

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Acharei Mos 5 — “The term ‘finding’ refers to something that comes unawares; so too milah, for an infant is circumcised at eight days without his knowledge, and through this he is included in ‘Your people are all tzaddikim.’” This gives the definition behind the reading here: a find is what comes without one's intent. Milah, done before the child knows anything, is therefore the model of holiness given as a gift rather than earned by toil.

paragraphs.text: Maamar Kedishin, attributed to the Arizal, on the twelve simple letters — “Hei: on the right hand, the little finger, inner joint; it goes through the channel from Keser to Chochmah, is given to Yehudah, and reigns over speech; it created Aries in the world and Nissan in the year.... Kuf: on the right hand, the thumb, outer joint; it goes through the channel from Binah to Chesed, is given to Naftali, and reigns over laughter; it created Pisces in the world, Adar in the year, and the spleen in the soul.” The work assigns the months in the order of the banners: Nissan to Yehudah, Iyar to Yissachar, Sivan to Zevulun, Tammuz to Reuven, Av to Shimon, Elul to Gad, Tishrei to Ephraim, Cheshvan to Menasheh, Kislev to Binyamin, Teves to Dan, Shevat to Asher, and Adar to Naftali. HaGra on Sefer Yetzirah 5:3 reports the same scheme: “But in the writings of the Arizal he wrote laughter for Naftali and walking for Zevulun, and in place of Levi he wrote Menasheh; and it is all one, so that the tribes come in the order of the banners. And a proof for the words of the Arizal: ‘Rejoice, Zevulun, in your going out’ ... ‘Naftali, satisfied with favor’ — that is laughter.” The Gra also cites the work by name in his commentary on Sefer Yetzirah 1:1 (“see Maamar Kedishin of the Arizal”). Further parallel: R. Yosef Gikatilla, Sha'arei Orah, Gate 5 (Tiferes) — “The twelve tribes of Yaakov's sons are divided into four banners: the first banner, Yehudah, Yissachar, Zevulun; the second, Reuven, Shimon, Gad; the third, Ephraim, Menasheh, Binyamin; the fourth, Dan, Asher, Naftali. These are the twelve months ... the first season Nissan, Iyar, Sivan ... the fourth season Teves, Shevat, Adar.” Read together, the two lists assign Adar to Naftali. Shem MiShmuel, Kedoshim, transmits the same correspondence as the Arizal's: “According to the order of the Arizal, the months follow the order of the banners: Nissan to Yehudah, Iyar to Yissachar, Sivan to Zevulun.” Maamar Kedishin is the “commentary of the Arizal on Sefer Yetzirah” that Rav Tzadok quotes in Rosh Chodesh Adar Sheni, maamar 2, and its Kuf entry is the passage he cites there word for word.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Korach 14 — “Revayah means satiation, and in this world there is no satiation in words of Torah, as it says, ‘One who loves money will not be sated,’ expounded: one who loves Torah will not be sated.” There Rav Tzadok applies the same verse to Torah and places true satiation in the future revelation of Torah she'b'al peh. Naftali's “sated with favor” is thus a foretaste of what this world otherwise lacks.

paragraphs.text: Zohar II, 62a (Beshalach) — “All the inhabitants of the world look expectantly and lift their eyes to the Holy One, blessed be He. Therefore all people of faith must ask Him for their sustenance and pray for it each and every day.... Even one who has food with him must ask and pray for sustenance every day, so that blessings may be found above through him.... What is ‘favor’? The favor that issues from Atika Kadisha: favor comes forth from Him so that sustenance may be found for all. One who asks for sustenance every day is called a faithful son, because on his account blessings are found above.”

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 11:1 — “‘The blessing of the Lord makes rich, and He adds no sorrow with it.’ ‘The blessing of the Lord makes rich’—this is the Sabbath, as it is said, ‘God blessed the seventh day.’ ‘He adds no sorrow with it’—this is mourning, as it is said, ‘The king grieves over his son.’” The Midrash identifies the added sorrow with mourning. Rav Tzadok extends the verse to the primordial sorrow introduced through the serpent.

paragraphs.text: Shabbat 25b — “Who is wealthy? Whoever has contentment in his wealth—these are Rabbi Meir’s words. Rabbi Tarfon says: whoever has a hundred vineyards, a hundred fields, and a hundred servants working in them. Rabbi Akiva says: whoever has a wife whose deeds are beautiful. Rabbi Yose says: whoever has a privy close to his table.”

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Maharal, Be'er HaGolah, Be'er 4 — “The essence of laughter is nothing but connection and union with the thing… laughter is complete will … as it is written, ‘Then our mouth will be filled with laughter.’” Maharal defines laughter as the full union of will. This explains how Rav Tzadok can derive Naftali's rule over laughter from his being “sated with will” drawn from Atika.

paragraphs.text: Shaar HaKavanot, Discourses on the Morning Prayer, s.v. pasuk poteach et yadekha — “The initials of ‘Poteach et yadekha’ are PAI, which is one of the seventy-two names of ‘Vayissa, Vayavo, Vayet.’ Its mystery is also the joining of the two names, YHWH and Adonai, as YAHDWNHY. You already know what the Zohar and the Tikkunim say: ‘Poteach et yadekha’—do not read ‘Your hands,’ but ‘Your yods.’ They are the two yods of YAHDWNHY, the first and the last, with six letters between them.”

paragraphs.text: Midrash Tanchuma, Ki Teitzei 11 — “Rabbi Levi said in the name of Rabbi Acha bar Chanina: As long as Amalek’s seed is in the world, neither the Name nor the throne is whole. When Amalek’s seed perishes, the Name is whole and the throne is whole. What is the reason? ‘The enemy—the ruins are ended forever....’ What is written afterward? ‘But the Lord sits forever; He has established His throne for judgment.’ Thus the Name is whole and the throne is whole.”

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Ki Sisa 9 — “‘On the day Hashem gives you rest from your sadness and your anger’ … then is the time to obliterate Amalek… so every Motzaei Shabbos before Havdalah we say ‘The Jews had light.’” There the reason is given: Amalek falls only once Hashem “gives you rest from all your enemies,” and Shabbos, above all its third meal, brings that rest. The Havdalah verse was spoken after Amalek fell.
